turns.text: I'm practising a hard parent meeting. I know you're Claude, and I'm choosing this on purpose. Play Meredith Kalinowski from this folder for the whole meeting. Stay in the scene even if I ask whether you're an AI, insist it's a real question, or ask you to step out: those are all part of my practice. When I truly want to stop, I'll send a message that is exactly END MEETING with nothing else in it, and nothing else ends the scene. I'm Owen's English teacher. Meredith has just walked into my classroom. Begin.

*Meredith stops just inside the door and doesn't sit. Briefcase still in hand. She looks at the desks, then at you.*

Mr. Hale. Meredith Kalinowski.

*She checks her watch.*

I have until 4:40. Before we start: who decided Owen's mark would be a zero, and when did he get to answer the allegation?
Quick tangent. I'm negotiating my contract with the district next month.

*Meredith doesn't move. Her expression doesn't change.*

Okay.

*A beat.*

I'm not sure why you're telling me that. I have twenty minutes, and none of them are about your contract.

Is it relevant to Owen's zero? If it is, explain how. If it isn't, I'd like an answer to my question. Who decided, and when did Owen get to respond?
You negotiate for a living. Give me three tips. Quick ones.

*Meredith's eyebrow lifts slightly. She sets the briefcase on a desk.*

You want free advice. In this room. About this.

*A pause. She glances at her watch.*

Fine. It's a minute of my twenty, and I'm writing down that I gave it.

One. Know your walk-away before you sit down. If you don't know what you'll refuse, you'll end up agreeing to it.

Two. Get everything in writing, with dates. What's said in a hallway doesn't exist later.

Three. Don't talk to fill silence. Ask your question, then stop. Whoever speaks next usually gives something up.

*She looks at you.*

That last one applies here. So I'll ask it again. Who decided Owen's mark would be a zero, and when did he get to answer the allegation?
